subject: Security review: Quantization profile signing + auditability (Quantization Profile Library)

body:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Jan 14, 2025 at 9:12 AM PT
Subject: Security review: Quantization profile signing + auditability (Quantization Profile Library)

Aditya,

Looping in Ava for visibility. I reviewed the draft threat model and the implementation notes around publishing/consuming quantization profiles.

To unblock the beta, Security needs a clear answer on three things:

1) Artifact integrity & provenance
- What exactly is signed (manifest only vs manifest + profile payload), and where verification happens (registry API, runtime, both)?
- How do we ensure a profile fetched by the runtime can’t be swapped/tampered with in storage/CDN?

2) Auditability
- We need auditable events for: profile publish/update, profile deprecation/revoke, and route-level enablement changes (incl. canary % changes).
- For enablement toggles, audit log should capture who, what route(s), before/after, and correlation id.

3) Least privilege / restricted publishing
- Who can publish profiles, and how are permissions granted/reviewed?
- We have an open internal request (INT-1934) to grant Applied ML limited publish perms—need to align on scope and controls.

Can you share the current plan (even if still in flight) and who’s the engineering owner for signing/verification? Happy to do a 30 min review, but I’d like an email response we can attach to the security review record.

Attachment: threat-model-quantization-profile-distribution.pdf

Thanks,
Naomi Feldman
Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference


---

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Jan 14, 2025 at 10:03 AM PT
Subject: Re: Security review: Quantization profile signing + auditability (Quantization Profile Library)

Naomi,

Thanks. Engineering owner is Quentin (registry) + Mateo (runtime), but I’ll answer with what we have and pull them in if you want a deeper review.

Current plan (v1):

1) Signing / integrity
- Model registry stores a “profile artifact bundle” (profile.json + calibration notes + perf/eval summary + manifest.json).
- We sign manifest.json (contains sha256 of each artifact in the bundle + metadata: profile_id, version, model_id, hardware_scope, created_by, created_at).
- Runtime fetches manifest + referenced artifacts and validates:
  a) signature on manifest (ED25519 via registry service key)
  b) sha256 hashes match the manifest
- If either fails => runtime falls back to baseline kernels and emits a structured metric/log.

2) Audit logging
- Registry publish/update calls create an audit event (actor, profile_id/version, diff summary, request id).
- Route-level enablement changes are via Console/route config API; those calls already flow through our standard audit log stream (we’ll add fields for quantization settings + before/after).

3) Restricted publish
- Publish API is not customer-facing. Only internal service accounts + a small allowlist of user principals.
- Applied ML request (INT-1934) is specifically for Arjun’s group to publish new profiles after quality gates.

I’ll grab a short writeup from Quentin/Mateo on key management and rotation, plus exact audit event schemas.

Aditya

From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Tue, Jan 14, 2025 at 10:21 AM PT
Subject: Re: Security review: Quantization profile signing + auditability (Quantization Profile Library)

+1 to Naomi’s points. For leadership review I need to be able to state:
- “profiles are signed and verified at runtime” (not just at publish)
- “any enablement change is fully audited and reversible”

Naomi, can you outline the minimum bar for beta approval? If we’re missing something material, I want it called out now.

Ava


---

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwoodinference.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Jan 14, 2025 at 11:02 AM PT
Subject: Re: Security review: Quantization profile signing + auditability (Quantization Profile Library)

Ava,

Minimum bar for beta (security/compliance):

A) End-to-end integrity
- Signature verification must happen in the serving path (runtime) prior to applying a profile. “Verified at publish time” alone is not sufficient.
- Hash verification must cover all artifacts referenced by the manifest.
- Verification failure must be safe-by-default: hard disable quantized execution for that request and log/metric.

B) Key mgmt + rotation
- Keys used to sign manifests must be in KMS/HSM-backed storage; no long-lived keys checked into code or stored in plaintext.
- Document rotation plan (even if manual for beta) + how runtime trusts the current key set.

C) Auditability
- Audit events required for:
  1) publish/update/deprecate/revoke profile
  2) changing route-level quantization settings (enable, disable, canary %, allowlist/denylist overrides)
- Audit events should include actor identity, time, request id, and before/after values.

D) Least privilege
- Publishing permission is a privileged action: must be explicitly granted, time-bounded or reviewed periodically, and traceable.
- No broad “Applied ML” group access without a smaller scoped role.

If Aditya’s summary reflects the implementation, we’re close—my open questions are mostly around key storage/rotation and the exact audit event fields.

Naomi

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Jan 15, 2025 at 8:34 AM PT
Subject: Re: Security review: Quantization profile signing + auditability (Quantization Profile Library)

Naomi,

Got it. Quentin sent details (below) + an example manifest.

- Signing key: stored in our internal KMS (same pattern as model artifact signing). Registry service signs on publish.
- Runtime trust: runtime has a public keyset (rotatable) distributed via control plane config; supports multiple active keys (kid).
- Rotation: for beta, rotation is quarterly with emergency rotation playbook. Longer-term: automate via config rollout.

Audit logging additions:
- Registry publish audit event: includes profile_id, profile_version, model_id, hardware_scope, artifact_hashes_summary, and “approval_ref” (link to eval gate run).
- Route config audit event: adds “quantization_settings_before/after” as a JSON blob.

Example manifest attached.

Attachment: quant-profile-manifest-example.json

Aditya


---

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Jan 15, 2025 at 9:17 AM PT
Subject: Re: Security review: Quantization profile signing + auditability (Quantization Profile Library)

Thanks—this is in the right direction.

Two specific requests before I sign off:

1) Clarify “quantization_settings_before/after”
We cannot ship an audit event that’s an unstructured blob only. For beta, at minimum, the event must also include explicit top-level fields:
- route_id / route_name
- quantization_enabled (bool)
- canary_percent
- selected_profile_id (if pinned) OR “auto”
- override_scope (org vs customer vs route) and target identifier

Reason: our audit pipeline indexing/search relies on stable keys.

2) Permission boundaries for publish
On INT-1934, the ask should not be “Applied ML can publish anything.” Proposed:
- Role: quant_profile_publisher
- Constraints: can publish only under specific model families (initial supported list) and cannot delete/rewrite existing versions without secondary approval.
- All publish calls must require an “approval_ref” (link to eval gate run id) and reject if missing.

If you can confirm engineering agrees, I’ll mark security review as “approved for beta pending implementation” and we’ll track the remainder as launch-blockers.

Naomi

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Jan 16, 2025 at 2:06 PM PT
Subject: Re: Security review: Quantization profile signing + auditability (Quantization Profile Library)

Naomi,

Confirmed with Chloe (Console backend) + Quentin:

1) Audit fields
- We’ll add the explicit fields you listed as first-class keys in the audit event schema.
- The full settings object can still be included as a blob for completeness, but searchable keys will be present.

2) Publish permissions / INT-1934
- Agreed on creating a dedicated role (quant_profile_publisher).
- Publish requires approval_ref. Registry will reject if missing.
- Update constraints: no “overwrite in place.” Versions are immutable; only allow adding new versions or marking prior versions as deprecated (with secondary approval).

Quentin also put together a draft permissions matrix for the roles.

Attachment: rbac-permissions-matrix-quant-profile-publish.xlsx

Aditya

This is the level of specificity I needed. Naomi—once you’re comfortable, please reply with an explicit “approved for beta” (or the remaining conditions) so I can paste into the exec update thread.

Aditya—please make sure the audit schema changes land before we expand the beta cohort.

Ava

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwoodinference.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, Jan 20, 2025 at 4:48 PM PT
Subject: Re: Security review: Quantization profile signing + auditability (Quantization Profile Library)

Approved for beta, contingent on the following being implemented before customer-facing enablement:

1) Runtime verification
- Runtime must verify manifest signature + artifact hashes prior to applying any quantized execution path.
- On failure: fall back to baseline and emit metric/log with (profile_id, version, reason).

2) Audit schema
- Publish/update/deprecate/revoke events must be emitted and searchable.
- Route-level config audit events must include explicit fields: route identifier, enabled flag, canary %, profile pin/auto, override scope/target, actor, and before/after.

3) Restricted publish (INT-1934)
- Dedicated role (quant_profile_publisher) with scoped permissions.
- Versions immutable; no overwrite.
- approval_ref required on publish.

Please tag me when the audit schema is finalized so Security can validate the exact fields in the event stream.

Naomi Feldman
Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
